facts.statement: Fallacosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Fallacosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period

facts.statement: Fossils of Fallacosteus have been found in the Gogo Formation in Kimberley, Western Australia.
facts.quote: found at the Gogo Formation of Kimberley, Western Australia

facts.statement: Fallacosteus turneri possessed an elongated snout that likely improved its hydrodynamic streamlining.
facts.quote: As with almost all other camuropiscids, F. turneri had an elongated snout that may have enhanced its hydrodynamic streamlining

facts.statement: The specific name turneri honors Sue Turner.
facts.quote: The specific name turneri honors Sue Turner

facts.statement: Fallacosteus belongs to the family Camuropiscidae, the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Fallacosteus is a member of the family Camuropiscidae under the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci

facts.statement: Fallacosteus was a marine genus described scientifically by Long in 1990.
facts.quote: Este género marino fue descrito científicamente por Long en 1990

facts.statement: Fallacosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
